firstPartyTitle: Dividing with Hundreds, Tens and Ones
goal: Represent division with base-ten blocks, exchange place-value units when needed, and explain equal sharing.

warmup.prompt: What can base-ten blocks tell you about the number 324 and sharing quantities?
warmup.supports: Invite models using hundreds, tens and ones; listen for exchanges.

steps: Model four hundreds, eight tens and eight ones.
Share the four hundreds into four equal groups, one hundred per group.
Share eight tens and eight ones: each group receives two tens and two ones.
Trade one hundred for ten tens and distribute one ten to each of eight groups.
Two tens remain: trade for twenty ones, then combine with four ones.
Share twenty-four ones among eight groups, giving three ones to each group.
Trade one hundred for ten tens, and distribute nine tens among nine equal groups.
Trade the remaining ten for ten ones and combine with the eight ones.
Share eighteen ones among nine groups, giving two ones to each.
Model nine tens and six ones.
Share eight tens among four groups, giving two tens per group; one ten remains.
Exchange remaining ten into ten ones, join with six ones and distribute sixteen ones: four ones to each group.
Represent eight tens and six ones.
Share eight tens among two groups, four tens to each.
Share six ones among two groups, three ones to each; each group contains forty-three.

independentEdulyticsCooldown.prompt: Show with base-ten blocks or a labelled block diagram how to divide 132 into six equal groups. Explain the exchanges.
teacherRubric: Regroup the hundred into ten tens and combine with three tens to make thirteen tens.
Give two tens to each of the six groups, leaving one ten.
Regroup the remaining ten into ten ones, add the original two ones and give two ones to each group.
Explain that each group contains twenty-two and that 6×22=132.

teacherOnly: Supply base-ten blocks and observe student grouping.
Compare diagrams and oral explanations; do not auto-grade original group work.
Source figures, any published artwork and original protected Cool-down are not copied.
